interesting: The museum's new exhibit is genuinely interesting for children and adults.
ones: particular items or people already mentioned or understood
The smaller phones sell better than the larger ones this year.
precisely: exactly; used to emphasize the exact reason for something
She arrived precisely on time for the interview, not a minute late.
category: a class or division of things sharing common characteristics
This product falls into a new category of eco-friendly packaging.
fits: is the right size, shape, or type for something
This solution fits our budget better than the other option.
everything: all things; the whole of something
Warmth speeds everything up, and dough rises quickly in a hot kitchen.
perfectly: in a perfect manner; completely or entirely
She remembered the song perfectly even though she had not sung it in years.
describing: saying what someone or something is like
She spent an hour describing her trip to her curious friends.
world: the earth and all its people and things
The trouble starts when the body's clock and the world's clock disagree.
had: past tense of have, used to show possession or a completed action
By the time she arrived, the shop had already closed.
stopped: came to an end or ceased moving
The rain finally stopped just before sunset.
awkward: There was an awkward silence after he forgot her name.
failures: instances of not succeeding or not working
Engineers studied past failures to design a safer bridge.
system: a set of things working together as a connected whole
The school introduced a new system for tracking student attendance.
names: words by which people, places or things are known
Old maps still show the original names of these villages.
evolution: the gradual development of species or ideas over time
They are evolution, caught in the act, right before our eyes.
act: to take action or do something
The government must act quickly before the crisis worsens.
